newsitem.title: USA: House ag panel chairman prods USDA for CRP rule.
newsitem.headline: House ag panel chairman prods USDA for CRP rule.

text.p: The chairman of the U.S. House Agriculture Commitee said Monday he would support extension of Conservation Reserve Program contracts if the Agriculture Department did not soon issue new operating rules.
The new CRP rules have been expected for weeks but were still under review at the White House budget office.
Bob Smith, an Oregon Republican, told reporters "obviously, it is past time for the decision to be made."
"I think we ought to take a look at the question of (crop loan) extension for six weeks," Smith said.
In its fiscal 1998 budget, the White House proposed giving USDA authority to extend the nine-month harvest-time loans for six months during times of low prices or transport snarls.
Speedy action is needed on CRP rules, Smith said, and told one questioner he would support a roll-over of contracts if the new regulation was not issued soon.
Thus far, Congress has blocked renewal of contracts although farmers are free to offer land for re-enrolment.
Contracts on 24 million acres expire this fall. By law, rental rates on new enrolment must be based on local cash rent. Some lawmakers worry Great Plains enrolment will drop.
